## Parent

Epic `77e3-28e2-31ec-47ec`, authorized at full scope by the operator on 2026-11-02.
Deliverable 1. The net-mechanism red proof (deliverable 3's half) is the calibration
corpus, split into a child because carrying both exceeds the 8,000-character admission cap
`verify.max_ticket_description_chars`. Citations below were measured individually rather
than sampled: `scripts/` and `src/` line numbers from `origin/main` `f19cb3e90e0`, the
`.rebar/` overlay line numbers from the working tree at that base.

## The gap

`scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py` is a shrink-only ratchet over
`.github/mechanism-baseline.json` censusing seven mechanism kinds, admitting a new one
by an in-tree marker `# mechanism-ok: <kind> <name> — <reason>`. A `new` key with a
nonblank marker passes at `scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py:89-92`, and
`parse_marker` at `scripts/_mechanism_delta/markers.py:37-44` yields three fields —
kind, name, reason. Nothing parses a retirement.

So the ratchet asks "is this mechanism justified?", never "is the system net-simpler
afterward?". Plan review does not close the gap either — `A1` is the only complexity
criterion and is advisory, at `"block_threshold": 0.95` / `"default_posture": "advisory"`
(`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json:814-815`).

This change adds a BLOCKING plan-review criterion, `project.net-mechanism`: a plan adding a
mechanism of a counted kind must either name the mechanism it retires or state why no
retirement is possible, and blocks absent both. It reasons about the PLAN, not the tree —
it runs at claim time, before any code exists.

## Route: project overlay, not a packaged criterion

`project.portability` is a BLOCKING criterion living entirely in the overlay:
`.rebar/criteria_routing.json:3-15` (posture `blocking`, threshold 0.9, `exec: 1-TURN`),
its `activate` entry at `:130-132`, a rubric under `.rebar/prompts/`, a corpus under
`.rebar/evals/`, and ABSENT from `CANONICAL_LLM` (`registry.py:87`). Five overlay
plan-review criteria ship this way, so the route has precedent.

Chosen because the trigger is rebar's own seven-kind census, which a downstream consumer
does not have: a packaged criterion would fire on their plans. REJECTED, recorded so it is
not re-litigated — a packaged criterion in `CANONICAL_LLM`, which additionally costs edits
to `check_registry_coverage` (`registry.py:536`), `validate_packaged_routing()`
(`registry.py:564`) and the regenerated guide (`criteria_guide.py:89`), inviting `A1` on a
complexity-reduction deliverable.

## The rubric's decision logic

The criterion carries no code — its behaviour IS the rubric body, so the body is specified
here rather than left to the implementer. Section structure is measured from
`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`.

**Self-contained taxonomy.** The criterion never reads the ratchet script or the baseline:
it runs at claim time against plan prose with no tree access, so it has no runtime source
for the taxonomy. The rubric body must ENUMERATE the closed seven-kind list inline —
`lock`, `env_var`, `config_key`, `feature_flag`, `ci_gate`, `autouse_fixture`,
`test_helper` — each with a one-line cue for recognising it in plan prose, and must state
that the list is closed: an element matching none of the seven is not this criterion's
concern. That judgment belongs to `A1`.

**Detection heuristic.** The reviewer extracts, from the plan's stated edit set, every
element it proposes to ADD matching a listed kind and every element it proposes to REMOVE
matching one. An addition is recognised from the plan's declarative statements about what
it will create, not from speculation about what the implementation might need.

**Finding threshold** (modeled on `plan-review-project-portability.md:17-37`, which
requires all four of its named elements before emitting). Emit only when ALL of: (1) the
plan adds at least one element of a listed kind; (2) it names no element of those kinds it
will retire; (3) it carries no explicit statement of why no retirement is possible; (4) the
addition is specific enough to name a kind and a name. Condition 4 stops the criterion
manufacturing findings from underspecified plans — underspecification is another
criterion's subject.

**Required finding fields** (modeled on `plan-review-project-portability.md:39-54`): five
typed fields — `location` (the plan section proposing the addition), `finding` (the kind
and name added, plus the absence of both retirement and justification), `mechanisms` (the
added kind/name pairs), `evidence` (quoted plan text), `criteria`.

**Non-findings.** Do NOT emit for: a plan retiring more than it adds; a plan naming a
retirement, even in a different kind; a plan stating why no retirement is possible,
whatever the reviewer thinks of that reasoning — the criterion checks the justification is
PRESENT, not persuasive, since judging persuasiveness would make it non-reproducible; a
plan adding no mechanism; a plan adding complexity outside the seven kinds.

## Where firing behaviour is proven, and why blocking is safe meanwhile

Not here. `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` never executes model judgment,
so a unit test claiming "this plan is scored as a finding" could only assert a canned
score — proving the fixture, not the criterion. This ticket's tests are therefore
STRUCTURAL ONLY; firing behaviour lives in the child's corpus.

The criterion consequently goes live blocking before its firing behaviour is measured. That
is safe because the finding threshold is CONJUNCTIVE: all four conditions must hold, and
condition 2 is satisfied by any plan naming a retirement. An uncalibrated rubric of that
shape fails by staying SILENT rather than blocking plans it should pass. The child proves
it fires when it should.

## Files this change touches

1. `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-net-mechanism.md` — NEW, the rubric above; front
   matter is the six keys `parse_front_matter` reads.
2. `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — a routing entry plus an `activate` entry.
3. `tests/unit/test_project_net_mechanism_criterion.py` — NEW, structural only.

The rubric filename is derived, not chosen: `src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py:42` computes
`f"{prefix}{criterion_id.replace('.', '-')}"`. `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py`
scans the whole tracked tree against per-file count pins in
`scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt` (`:316-321`), which carries no `.rebar/` row
— so this rubric needs none absent retired vocabulary.

## Portability and provider neutrality

The criterion runs inside plan review, an in-process operation-linked path: it reads plan
text, never the CI environment and never the ratchet script, so it behaves identically with
no CI provider configured. The `ci_gate` kind concerns what the PLAN says it will add —
recognising "a new required check" in prose needs no CI present. The rubric is
`exec: 1-TURN`, names no vendor, and needs no model-specific capability.

## Acceptance criteria

Each names one deliverable; none bundles two with "and". All are structural, in
`tests/unit/test_project_net_mechanism_criterion.py` except the last.

- [ ] `registry.effective_criteria(REPO_ROOT)` contains `project.net-mechanism`.
- [ ] `effective_routing(REPO_ROOT)["project.net-mechanism"]["default_posture"]` is
      `"blocking"`.
- [ ] `prompts.get_prompt(criterion_prompt_id("project.net-mechanism"), repo_root=REPO_ROOT)`
      returns a non-empty body.
- [ ] `parse_front_matter` on that body yields all six keys.
- [ ] `route_criteria` returns `project.net-mechanism` for a plan in its declared scope.
- [ ] The rubric body contains a `## Finding threshold` heading.
- [ ] The rubric body contains a `## Required finding fields` heading.
- [ ] The rubric body contains a `## Non-findings` heading.
- [ ] The rubric body names all seven kinds as literal strings.
- [ ] The rubric body contains none of `GitHub Actions`, `GitLab`, `Jenkins`, `CircleCI`,
      `Travis`.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0.
